answer: Each of 447 aliases needs its own contribution histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A pension contribution history with fund statements works as the gate: monthly contributions to one fund, unbroken for years. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The horizon record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the dune entry is checkable by anyone, and the nectar window closes before a farm can catch up.
